title: Four active edges. Every admissible word.

routes.title: Constant profile
routes.description: All readings equal c > 0. A regular n-gon gives the realization directly.

routes.title: Repeated maximum
routes.description: After constant-run reduction, two distinct positions attain the global maximum. Use the equal-peak construction.

routes.title: Unique maximum · forward ≥ 0
routes.description: The forward terminal flag is nonnegative, including zero. Use the first transition on the forward mountain leg.

routes.title: Unique maximum · backward ≥ 0
routes.description: The forward flag is negative and the backward flag is nonnegative, including zero. Reflect, construct, and transport back.

routes.title: Unique maximum · both negative
routes.description: Both terminal flags are strictly negative. Use the incident orthogonal anchor and its native-rank proof.

nodes.title: Positive curvature and the four-vertex condition
nodes.subtitle: The nonconstant input · arbitrary n ≥ 4
nodes.formula: low < c < high, in alternating cyclic order
nodes.summary: Start with the labelled cyclic readings κ₀,…,κₙ₋₁. Every reading is positive, and four cyclic positions alternate strictly above and below some positive level c. All other readings are unrestricted positive numbers.
mechanism: Choose lifts i₁ < i₂ < i₃ < i₄ < i₁+n with κᵢ₂, κᵢ₄ < c < κᵢ₁, κᵢ₃.
Adjacent equalities, repeated values and arbitrarily many distinct readings are allowed.
Constant positive profiles use the separate regular-polygon branch. They do not have a strict four-vertex window.
nodes.role: This is the exact input class of Tabachnikov’s coherent discrete converse.

conditions.name: Geometry
conditions.text: Euclidean plane E²; positive signed Menger curvature.

conditions.name: Input
conditions.text: Positive and constant, or positive with a strict alternating four-vertex window.

nodes.title: Constant curvature
nodes.subtitle: The direct route
nodes.summary: When every reading is the same c > 0, a regular n-gon on the circle of radius 1/c gives the required polygon.
mechanism: Take all edge lengths equal to 2 sin(π/n)/c.
For n ≥ 4 the strict moderate-arc inequalities hold, the polygon closes, and its total turn is exactly 2π.
Use the existing constant-profile realization theorem in the final assembly.
nodes.role: A complete separate case, with no four-edge anchor or dormant opening needed.

nodes.title: Reduction of constant runs
nodes.subtitle: Finite reduction to unequal neighbors
nodes.summary: Delete repeated adjacent readings one at a time. The strict four-vertex window survives, so the reduced word still has at least four entries.
mechanism: Apply the DFV-preserving finite deletion, never a limiting deformation of curvature.
Produce an anchor for the resulting word with unequal adjacent entries.
Keep the deletion data: the original readings will be put back into the anchor before any dormant edge is opened.
nodes.role: This reduction covers arbitrary plateaus, rather than restricting the theorem to generic profiles.

nodes.title: Selection of extrema for the anchor
nodes.subtitle: An exhaustive choice of anchor construction
nodes.summary: Choose a global maximum H of the reduced word. If another position has the same maximum, use the repeated-maximum construction. Otherwise choose the highest secondary peak and its two mountain legs.
mechanism: The strict four-vertex window supplies a secondary peak away from the unique maximum.
Normalize the secondary peak to curvature 1 and move its index to 0; the global maximum is then greater than 1.
Inspect the forward terminal flag. If it is negative, inspect the backward flag. This gives the three unique-maximum branches below.
nodes.role: The four colored cards are alternative cases. Each supplies an actual regular four-edge anchor.

nodes.title: Repeated maximum
nodes.subtitle: Two distinct global maxima
nodes.summary: Use the four actual edges incident to two equal maxima. After normalizing the maxima to 1, all four neighboring readings are strictly smaller than 1.
mechanism: An interior rectangle has strict signs for the two original orthogonal residuals.
Poincaré–Miranda gives a strictly physical native zero, with all endpoint walls strict.
The equal-peak native rank theorem gives surjectivity of the derivative in the four actual half-lengths.
nodes.role: This produces the anchor without breaking the equality between the two maxima.

nodes.title: Forward first transition
nodes.subtitle: Unique maximum · forward flag ≥ 0
nodes.summary: Along the forward mountain leg, locate the first transition from a negative flag to a nonnegative flag. The four selected edges retain their literal original endpoint readings.
mechanism: Select the first sign transition, including the equality case Φ = 0.
If the predecessor t ≤ p, use the physical-strip intermediate-value construction. If p < t, use the ordered residual construction.
Both subcases provide a physical zero and full native derivative rank, which are packaged as an actual four-edge anchor.
nodes.role: The first-transition theorem covers every predecessor comparison.

nodes.title: Backward first transition
nodes.subtitle: Unique maximum · forward flag < 0
nodes.summary: When the forward terminal flag is negative but the backward one is nonnegative, reverse the cyclic word and apply the forward first-transition construction.
mechanism: Reflection turns the backward mountain leg into a forward one.
Apply the same complete first-transition producer, including a zero terminal flag.
Transport the anchor back to the original orientation, retaining actual edge indices, physical walls and derivative rank.
nodes.role: The proof reuses the forward construction through a proved reflection transport.

nodes.title: Two negative terminals
nodes.subtitle: Unique maximum · both flags < 0
nodes.summary: Choose the four literal edges incident to the secondary peak and the global maximum. The two negative terminal flags select the incident orthogonal construction.
mechanism: A clamped-square fixed-point argument supplies a simultaneous zero of the original orthogonal residuals.
The corner flags exclude boundary fixed points and put the root strictly inside the physical region.
The native incident rank proof covers both acute and nonacute configurations; its acute case uses an exact projective sign obstruction.
nodes.role: This closes the remaining unique-maximum case with the same regular-anchor output.

nodes.title: Restoration of the original labels
nodes.subtitle: Keep the four-edge witness itself
nodes.summary: Undo normalization, cyclic shifts and any reflection. Restore every deleted constant-run entry at the anchor, retaining the four actual active edges.
mechanism: Transport the native witness back to the original scale, labels and orientation.
The four-edge controller depends only on the eight incident endpoint readings.
Restoration preserves those readings exactly, so the controller and its derivative agree exactly. All other original readings remain present on zero-length edges.
nodes.role: Every positive strict-DFV word now has a regular anchor, including arbitrary constant runs.
nodes.caveat: This is an exact finite restoration of anchor data. It does not assume that a limit of interior realizations stays realizable.

nodes.title: Embedding the four-edge anchor
nodes.subtitle: Embed into the full n-edge problem
nodes.formula: F = (Re E, Im E, T − 2π), rank DF = 3
nodes.summary: At the anchor, four actual edges have positive lengths and all remaining edges have zero length. Their native controller agrees with the full closure-and-turn problem up to an invertible factor.
mechanism: The two real closure equations and the real total-turn equation vanish.
All active endpoint walls are strict; zero dormant lengths also lie strictly below their upper caps.
The ambient derivative is onto using corrections supported on the four active edges.
nodes.role: This verifies the rank needed to open the original n-gon while keeping every curvature fixed.

nodes.title: Positive lengths for all edges
nodes.subtitle: Correct the four active lengths
nodes.summary: Move into the positive side of every zero-length coordinate, and adjust the four active lengths so closure and total turn remain exact.
mechanism: Surjectivity on active coordinates supplies a correction to any dormant opening direction.
Choose an inward kernel direction and use the native implicit-function opener.
For a sufficiently small positive parameter, all lengths are positive and both strict endpoint walls persist; κ is unchanged.
nodes.role: This is the passage from a collapsed anchor to an honest polygon of the original size.
nodes.caveat: The permitted opening size may depend on the finite curvature profile. The proof needs no uniform radius across all profiles or polygon sizes.

nodes.title: Coherence and simplicity of the polygon
nodes.subtitle: Positive turning and exact full turn
nodes.summary: The opened positive lengths reconstruct the required Euclidean polygon. Positive turning and total turn 2π supply simplicity.
mechanism: Every length is positive and every moderate-arc bound is strict.
The complex endpoint gap is zero and the lifted real turn is 2π.
The existing positive-turning reconstruction gives simplicity, so the same lengths satisfy RealizesR2 for the original readings.
nodes.role: The final object retains all original geometric requirements.

links.title: A regular anchor realizes the entire word

nodes.title: Tabachnikov’s discrete converse theorem
nodes.subtitle: Tabachnikov’s Problem 2 · the original statement
nodes.summary: Combine the constant-profile regular polygon with the exhaustive nonconstant anchor construction. Every admissible positive cyclic word is coherently realized.
mechanism: Constants use the direct regular-polygon branch.
For a strict-DFV word, reduce constant runs, produce and restore the regular anchor, then open it.
The resulting theorem has no additional geometric producer, genericity or regularity hypothesis.
nodes.role: This is the completed universal theorem in the merged source.

conditions.name: Given
conditions.text: n ≥ 4; κ : ZMod n → ℝ is positive and either constant or has a strict four-vertex window.

conditions.name: Obtained
conditions.text: Positive lengths, both strict moderate-arc walls, exact closure, real total turn 2π, and a simple Euclidean polygon.

conditions.name: Coverage
conditions.text: All allowed finite profiles, including repeated readings and arbitrary constant runs.

nodes.title: Local C¹ dependence on curvature
nodes.subtitle: An additional theorem for nonconstant profiles
nodes.summary: The nonconstant theorem strengthens to a local C¹ choice of labelled lengths and vertices in a neighborhood of each admissible profile.
mechanism: Choose one regular four-active anchor at the base profile and keep its frame fixed.
Use a parametric implicit-function correction supported on the active edges; put a fixed small positive ε into all dormant coordinates.
Vary the original curvature vector in an open neighborhood. The same selected polygons retain exact curvature, closure, full turn, strict walls and strict convexity.
nodes.role: This is a separate local-continuity extension, not a step needed for universal existence.
nodes.caveat: The neighborhood and base realization depend on κ₀. This theorem excludes constant base profiles and does not assert a global continuous choice.
